meta.name: CATSKILLS-SSTO
meta.description: Pure geometry / topology assembly. Drop-in modules mate at named ports.
meta.architecture: Drop-ins each with own skid and bay doors: cargo, Fusion electric plant, combined-cycle engine. Plant ↔ engine by power cable (DEC → bus coupler). Tail bolts to fuselage around the engine nozzle cutout; nozzle belongs to the engine only.
meta.skids: Cargo, Fusion power plant, and combined-cycle engine are separate drop-in packages.
meta.outliner_check: CHARM owns Magnet/RF/Drive/Thermal sub-racks (bolt into CHARM before skid drop-in); skid owns PSU + cryo compressor + fuel + DEC + battery. INTERIM: DEC He ash dumps into fusion plant bay atmosphere (pollutes bay).
meta.charm_cad: CHARM expands to left fusion chamber | heat exchange chamber | right fusion chamber + central axis — match Fisch multi-chamber centrifugal mirror figure.
meta.packaging: CHARM owns Magnet/RF/Drive/Thermal sub-racks (bolt into CHARM before skid drop-in); skid owns PSU + cryo compressor + fuel + DEC + battery. INTERIM: DEC He ash dumps into fusion plant bay atmosphere (pollutes bay).
meta.ash_handling: interim_bay_pollution: He ash after DEC → fusion_plant_bay_atmosphere; not freeze/liquefy hazard; replace with buffer+purge later.
meta.engine_sizing: P1=65MW P2=P3=995MW meng=15t; Plan A TA m_pl=0 m_dry~172t mw~39t Isp=2000s
meta.figure_ssot: Paper mermaid figures must match this assembly.json; ground cart / vacuum pack / plant bus added from paper schematic.
meta.engine_air_path: freestream → twin OMS-shoulder scoops → cross-duct plenum → (EDF | stage-2) → shared flared nozzle; belly boat unpierced; aft RCS retained
meta.plan_a: no cargo; m_land~190t; S~480m2; b~33m; airport KEDW 4572m; carbon sandwich + reusable TPS only (arxiv.md §1.2b)

heritage_orbiter_oml.note: Kitbash DNA / FG mesh; Plan A envelope span/area sized to plant (arxiv.md §1.2b)

children.label: Fuselage
children.note: Structural boat: open cradle plus the pieces that permanently live on it — nose landing gear and the two aft space-steering pods. Forward steering is on the crew capsule, not here. Includes the Shuttle-style body flap on the aft belly.

children.label: Fuselage cradle
children.note: Open boat / long cradle. Drop-in wells for crew, airlock, cargo bay, CHARM power plant, and combined-cycle engine. Belly wing saddle + nose-gear saddle. Aft steering pods bolt to this cradle; forward steering rides on the crew capsule.

Open mid-body well; Cargo Bay (skid+doors) drops in as one unit
Open well for Fusion electric plant drop-in (~33.3–45 m)
Open aft well for combined-cycle engine drop-in (~45–52 m, with water + tail)
Belly saddle / pinch for one-piece wing
Local saddle / dimple in the fuselage cradle belly. Nose landing gear bolts up into this hardpoint (same idea as the wing saddle, smaller).
Aft hardpoint for vertical stabilizer. Bolts around the engine nozzle cutout — nozzle pokes out underneath; Tail does not attach to the nozzle.
Body flap hinge on aft cradle belly

children.label: Nose landing gear
children.note: Isolated nose wheel. Bolts to a saddle/dimple on the fuselage cradle belly — not buried in a closed well as primary structure language.

children.note: Shuttle-style left aft pod: OMS engines deleted; shoulder scoop + full RCS nozzle set. Internal LMP-103S / He / manifold feed Bradford/ECAPS-class thrusters at heritage ports. Bolts to fuselage cradle.

children.label: Right aft steering pod
children.placement: aft fuselage, right of tail fin (Shuttle OMS/RCS pod)
children.note: Shuttle-style right aft pod: OMS engines deleted; shoulder scoop + full RCS nozzle set. Internal LMP-103S / He / manifold feed Bradford/ECAPS-class thrusters at heritage ports. Bolts to fuselage cradle.

children.label: Right aft LMP-103S tank
children.note: ADN-based green monopropellant for aft primary+vernier banks. OMS hypergol deleted.

children.label: Right aft He pressurant
children.note: Helium pressurant for LMP-103S feed.

children.label: Right aft RCS manifold
children.note: Feed/isolation manifold to Bradford/ECAPS-class thruster banks.

children.label: Right aft primary RCS bank
children.note: Heritage nozzle locations/counts; green mono thrusters behind existing ports. Attitude only.

children.label: Body flap
children.note: Shuttle-style single body flap on the aft fuselage belly — pitch trim and engine-bell thermal shield on entry. Hinged to the fuselage cradle, not part of the Tail assembly.

children.label: Crew capsule
children.note: Drop-in collection: pressure vessel (with interior) plus side hatch and forward steering module bolted to the vessel. Drops into the forward cradle well.

children.label: Pressure vessel
children.note: Standalone pressure vessel (Crew Dragon–like cabin, stretched). All ECLSS / O2 / N2 / seats / galley / WCS / luggage live INSIDE this shell. Solid pressure hatch aft (to airlock) and solid port side hatch (Earth/runway only). Side hatch and forward steering module bolt onto this vessel as siblings.

ports.note: Nose hardpoint on pressure vessel for forward steering module

children.label: Living / systems cabin
children.note: Open single-deck cabin (stretched Crew Dragon vibe). Flight deck CDR+PLT facing forward; six forward-facing passenger seats in three rows of two with a center aisle. WCS (space toilet, no 1g bathroom suite). Galley = food / pouch station — NO kitchen sink (0g). Luggage locker doors face into the cabin aisle. ECLSS + O2/N2 underfloor or cabin-side INSIDE the pressure shell. Clear aisle to closed aft pressure hatch.

children.label: Six passenger seats
children.note: Six passenger seats aft of flight deck, all facing forward (Crew Dragon–like). Not sideways facing pairs.

children.label: Toilet (WCS)
children.note: Space waste collection system with aisle access; not a 1g bathroom suite.

children.label: Galley / food station (no sink)
children.note: Crew Dragon–style food system: retort meal pouches in stowage bags/trays, compact food warmer, potable-water rehydration interface. No kitchen sink, no restaurant galley box.

children.label: Luggage lockers
children.note: Deep cargo-bay-style stowage (Dragon under-seat / sidewall cargo volume class) — not thin wall panels. Doors open into the cabin aisle.

children.label: Life-support rack
children.note: Inside the pressure vessel (Crew Dragon: much ECLSS underfloor / cabin). Never outside the vacuum shell.

children.label: Aft pressure hatch door (to airlock)
children.note: Solid closable pressure door on the aft bulkhead of the crew pressure vessel. Mates to airlock forward hatch. Must show as a real door, not an empty hole.

children.label: Left-side ground hatch (runway only)
children.note: Solid closable side hatch in the pressure-vessel skin for Earth/runway ingress. Not an open hole; not vacuum-rated as an outer space hatch.

children.label: Forward steering module (nose)
children.note: Nose RCS module: Shuttle nozzle locations/counts retained; LMP-103S green monoprop + Bradford/ECAPS-class thrusters. Bolts to pressure-vessel nose; not inside pressurized volume.

children.label: Forward LMP-103S tank
children.note: Nose RCS green monopropellant store.

children.label: Forward primary RCS bank
children.note: Heritage nose nozzle locations/counts; attitude / abort only.

children.label: Airlock
children.note: Drop-in collection: pressure vessel (suited standing room) plus the two pressure doors, air tank, and pressurization gadgets. Hatches only to crew and cargo — submarine / ISS style.

children.label: Pressure vessel
children.note: Suited standing chamber (~2 people). Physical pressurized shell of the airlock. Doors, air tank, and cycle gadgets bolt to this vessel.

children.label: Door between cabin and airlock
children.note: Pressure door on the forward face of the airlock pressure vessel (crew side).

children.label: Door between airlock and cargo bay
children.note: Pressure door on the aft face of the airlock pressure vessel (cargo-bay side).

children.label: Air tank (press / depress)
children.note: Stores air to repressurize the chamber after vacuum; accepts dump/bleed during depress.

children.label: Pressurization gadgets
children.note: Valves, pump/equalizer, gauges, and controls to pressurize and unpressurize the chamber (ISS / submarine airlock style).

children.label: Cargo bay
children.note: Drop-in collection: cargo skid plus its own left/right doors. The fuselage cradle is open here — doors are not fuselage skin; they come with the bay.

children.label: Cargo skid
children.note: Plan A TA: bay skid carries plant support / empty cargo role deferred (m_pl=0). Doors hinge to this skid; skid sits in the fuselage cradle well. No pressure door aft — EVA into the open CHARM / engine wells for maintenance.

children.label: Fusion electric plant
children.note: Fusion plant: skid + finished CHARM island (with its own sub-racks + permanent shield bulkhead) + Magnet PSU bay + cryo compressor bay + fuel + DEC + battery + water tanks (relocated ahead of CHARM as a supplemental shield, arxiv.md §9.9). Skid grew from 11.7 m to 15.7 m to hold the relocated water tank.

children.label: Fusion plant skid
children.note: Drop-in frame + bay doors + bay volume. INTERIM: He ash from DEC is allowed to pollute this bay atmosphere until a proper dump/purge is designed.

children.label: Skid structure
children.note: Skid rails. Seats: CHARM island mounts, Magnet PSU bay, cryo compressor bay, fuel services, DEC, flight battery, water tanks (relocated ahead of CHARM, arxiv.md §9.9).

children.label: Left fusion plant bay door
children.note: Hinged to fusion plant skid (not fuselage).

children.label: Right fusion plant bay door
children.note: Hinged to fusion plant skid (not fuselage).

children.label: Fusion plant bay atmosphere
children.note: INTERIM ash sink: after DEC takes the energy, He ash is dumped into the sealed fusion-plant bay volume (pollutes the bay). Not a finished design — no dedicated vent hole yet; later replace with controlled buffer → ground/orbit purge. He will not freeze/liquefy when the bay is eventually opened.

children.label: CHARM
children.note: CHARM assembly = permanent shield bulkhead (forward face) + backbone + chamber string + four CHARM-owned sub-racks (Magnet, RF, Rotation drive, Thermal). Each rack is built separately and bolted into CHARM before the finished island integrates into the fusion plant skid.

children.label: Permanent shield bulkhead
children.note: arxiv.md §9.9 (B1): permanent polyethylene/borated-polyethylene bulkhead spanning the fuselage cross-section, sized for zero water present (photon + residual-neutron order-of-magnitude attenuation, NIST XCOM + standard fast-neutron removal cross sections). Forward face of CHARM, immediately aft of the fuel bay — blocks CHARM radiation from reaching the relocated water tank, fuel, battery, cargo, airlock, and crew even when the water tank is empty. Mass is carved out of the existing unsized RF/shield/structure remainder inside m_C (does not add to m_C=66.7 t).

ports.note: Bolts to fuel_services_frame / skid rails on the forward side
Bolts to charm_backbone on the aft side

children.label: CHARM backbone / strongback
children.note: Machine strongback that the chamber string and CHARM-owned sub-racks bolt to. Built first; racks integrate onto it; finished CHARM island then seats on the plant skid.

children.label: Chamber string
children.note: Vacuum vessel string: left fusion | heat exchange | right fusion + central axis. Primary CHARM build article; Magnet / RF / Drive / Thermal racks bolt onto this + backbone.

children.label: Left fusion chamber
children.note: CHARM outer fusion chamber (port). Boron centrifugally trapped on the outer wall; p-¹¹B fusion region. Hot He / hot protons flow inward to the heat-exchange chamber.

children.label: Heat exchange chamber
children.note: Central CHARM chamber. Receives hot He and hot protons from both fusion chambers; He extracted with waves; energy path toward DEC. Cold He / cold proton returns as on the Fisch slide.

ports.note: Ash / charged-product face to DEC collector

children.label: Right fusion chamber
children.note: CHARM outer fusion chamber (starboard). Mirror of the left chamber — same centrifugal boron trap and fusion role.

children.label: Central axis / shaft
children.note: Common rotation / alignment axis through left fusion — heat exchange — right fusion (plugs at both ends on the Fisch CHARM figure).

children.label: Magnet rack
children.note: CHARM-owned sub-rack: mirror coils + on-coil cryostats/cold heads. Built as a unit, bolted onto the CHARM backbone around the fusion chambers. Power leads come later from the skid Magnet PSU; cryogen from the skid compressor.

children.label: Magnet rack frame
children.note: Separately buildable frame; bolts to CHARM backbone at magnet_rack_mount.

children.label: Mirror magnets
children.note: Mirror / chamber field coils — live in the CHARM Magnet rack, seated on the fusion chamber ODs. N_coil=6, 1.8 t each (10.8 t total), WHAM-anchored (arxiv.md §9.6, refs [34]-[36]); on-coil cold head mass is bundled into mass_each_t.

children.label: Magnet cryostats / cold heads
children.note: Cryostat jackets and cold heads — part of the CHARM Magnet rack (what is cryocooled).

size.note: Bottom-up known mass (magnets only; rack frame not independently sized). See arxiv.md §9.6.

children.label: RF rack
children.note: CHARM-owned sub-rack: neck RF launchers + adjacent amplifier modules. Built separately, bolted into CHARM at the chamber necks before plant integration.

children.label: RF rack frame
children.note: Separately buildable frame; bolts to CHARM backbone at rf_rack_mount.

children.label: RF launchers / neck antennas
children.note: Ponderomotive / one-way RF wall launchers at the necks — owned by the CHARM RF rack.

children.label: RF amplifier modules
children.note: RF amp modules in the CHARM RF rack, short-waveguided to the neck launchers.

children.label: Rotation drive rack
children.note: CHARM-owned sub-rack: rotation / ExB drive hardware. Built separately, bolted to the CHARM axis / backbone — not a skid cabinet.

children.label: Rotation drive rack frame
children.note: Separately buildable frame; bolts to CHARM backbone at drive_rack_mount.

children.label: Rotation drive
children.note: Rotation / ExB drive — gear in the CHARM Rotation drive rack, couples into the central axis.

children.label: Thermal rack
children.note: CHARM-owned sub-rack: local coolant bath and on-machine thermal plumbing at the HEX. Built separately and bolted into CHARM; fed by the skid cryo compressor bay.

children.label: Thermal rack frame
children.note: Separately buildable frame; bolts to CHARM backbone at thermal_rack_mount.

children.label: Coolant bath
children.note: Local coolant / thermal bath — owned by the CHARM Thermal rack, looped to the HEX and magnet cryostats.

children.label: DEC
children.note: Direct energy conversion: alpha / charged-product collector and wave couplers. Takes ordered alpha energy onto the electrical bus. Remaining neutral He ash is INTERIM-dumped into the fusion plant bay atmosphere (careless placeholder — not a flight ash system).

ports.note: Collector / wave-coupler face toward CHARM ash chamber
1 GW-class electrical bus → propulsion bus coupler
Neutral He ash after energy extraction — currently dumped to plant bay (interim)

children.label: Plant electrical bus (1 GW)
children.note: Named plant-side bus after DEC. Flight product power leaves via power cable to the propulsion bus coupler on the engine skid.

children.label: Magnet PSU bay
children.note: Skid power-electronics bay for the Magnet PSU. Coils are on CHARM.

children.label: Magnet PSU
children.note: Magnet power supply electronics (current / quench protection). 'Magnet services' means this cabinet — NOT the magnets. Coils + cryostats stay on CHARM; thick leads run from this PSU to the coils.

children.label: Cryo compressor bay
children.note: Skid compressor plant. Cold heads live on CHARM magnets. Sized in arxiv.md §9.6: N_AL630=6 flight-remanufactured Cryomech AL630-class compressor packages (×1.5 flight-mass guess, ×1.4 integration margin) → 2.41 t, 87.6 kW electrical, 600 W @ 20 K total (3.6% of the CHARM island mass budget). Conservative SPARC-TFMC-anchored risk case (24-48 units, 8-16 t) and NASA flight-cryocooler ceiling case (45-90 t) also carried in §9.6.

children.label: Cryo compressor plant
children.note: Helium / cryogen COMPRESSOR and oil management — the noisy plant package on the skid. It does NOT cryocool the magnets by itself; short cryogen lines feed the magnet cold heads and bath on the CHARM island. count=6 (one dedicated compressor package per magnet); mass/power in size block are flight-remanufactured-from-ground-hardware estimates, see arxiv.md §9.6.

children.label: Vacuum / controls pack
children.note: Roughing/turbo vacuum, gauges, and local plant controls for the chamber string. Bolts to the fusion plant skid; pumps the CHARM vacuum envelope.

children.label: Fuel services
children.note: Plant consumables bay on the skid: proton tank, ¹¹B container, solid injector. Feeds both fusion chambers; not inside the vacuum core.

children.label: Proton tank
children.note: Gaseous H₂ / proton feedstock. Plumbing line to CHARM proton injector.

children.label: Boron-11 container
children.note: Solid ¹¹B store (pellets/powder). Feeds the solid-fuel injector — not piped as a gas.

children.label: Boron-11 solid fuel injector
children.note: Meters / vaporizes / ionizes solid ¹¹B into the CHARM rotating boron chamber. This is the wire from boron store into CHARM.

children.label: Flight battery
children.note: Flight battery (~2 t): on-orbit relight / hotel — magnets + RF (+ rotation) kindling. First light on Earth uses the ground cart (not carried).

children.label: Water tanks (space propellant)

ports.note: Long cross-skid duct run to the water injector on the combined-cycle engine (~10 m; was a short in-skid run when the tank lived aft of CHARM)

children.note: Stage-3 reaction mass only. Reference mw≈44.3 t ≈44 m³ liquid water at Isp=2000 s (166 t if Isp=665 s demo; 27 t if Isp=3150 s MPD-class). RELOCATED (arxiv.md §9.9, B2) from aft-of-CHARM / engine skid to ahead of CHARM on the fusion plant skid: supplemental radiation shield when full, on top of the permanent charm_shield_bulkhead which holds when empty. Envelope x=35.5–39.5 m (same 4 m length) must visually dominate the plant skid bay — not small service bottles.

children.label: Ground cart (Earth only)
children.note: Airport / pad umbilical cart for first light. Not carried. Supplies startup power to Magnet PSU / RF / cryo on the ground; flight relight uses the flight battery.

children.label: Combined-cycle engine
children.note: Three-stage electric CC: P1*≈65 MW, P2*=P3*≈995 MW. meng=15 t budget (EDF 5 + air-plasma 4.4 + water 3.1 + shared 2.5). Power cable from fusion plant only. Water tanks moved OFF this skid to the fusion plant skid (arxiv.md §9.9); fed here by a long cross-skid duct (j_water_to_injector).

children.label: Engine skid
children.note: Collection: skid structure plus its left/right bay doors. Expand to see doors; propulsion hardware lives on the Combined-cycle engine beside this skid.

children.label: Skid structure
children.note: Physical drop-in propulsion frame. Bay doors hinge here; engine hardware bolts here. Sits in the aft fuselage cradle well. Nozzle exits under Tail. Water tanks no longer mount here (moved to charm_skid, arxiv.md §9.9) — water arrives via a long duct to the water_injector instead.

ports.note: Receives CHARM DEC bus via power cable

children.label: Left engine bay door
children.note: Hinged to combined-cycle engine skid (not fuselage).

children.label: Right engine bay door
children.note: Hinged to combined-cycle engine skid (not fuselage).

children.label: Stage-1 electric ducted fan
children.note: Stage-1 electric ducted fan (HEMM-class). Lives IN the inlet duct behind the external air scoops — not a freestanding fan on the skid face. Outside air: scoops → inlet duct → fan face → bypass → shared flared nozzle. P1*≈65 MW at m0=240 t; mass budget ≈5.0 t.

children.label: Stage-2 microwave air plasma jet
children.note: Stage 2: P2*≈995 MW sizes P_star. Electrothermal T/P≈0.83 N/kW (not Ye 28 N/kW). Mass budget ≈4.4 t ⇒ packaging unobtainium ~230 kW/kg. Free air.

children.label: Air precompressor / ram conditioner
children.note: Raises ingested air toward microwave-breakdown / applicator pressure (ram +/or electric boost).

children.label: Microwave source farm (magnetron / solid-state)
children.note: High-power microwave generators for stage-2 air plasma (and can feed stage-3 source). Lab anchor ~2.45 GHz magnetron [Ye 2020]; flight is an array / high-power farm.

children.label: Microwave air applicator / plasma duct
children.note: Waveguide / quartz-ceramic duct where microwaves ionize and heat compressed air (>1000 °C class in lab).

children.label: Stage-3 water plasma rack
children.note: Stage 3: P3*≈995 MW → T3≈56 kN at Isp=2000 s, η_jet=0.55. Water mw≈44 t for Δv=4 km/s. Mass budget ≈3.1 t. Lit: Nakagawa water MW ion; Komatsu water MPD; Brandenburg water MET.

children.label: Water vaporizer / gas-liquid separator
children.note: Turns liquid water feed into vapor for the microwave plasma source (smallsat water thruster feed practice).

children.label: Stage-3 water plasma thruster
children.note: Stage 3 (intakes sealed): water vapor → microwave H₂O plasma → accelerate/expand. Architecture lineage: miniature microwave water ion thrusters (Nakagawa/Koizumi); vehicle sizes from CHARM GW bus (scale-up unobtainium).

children.label: Water injector
children.note: Meters carried water into the stage-3 vaporizer / thruster when intakes are sealed.

children.label: Propulsion bus coupler
children.note: Engine-side end of the CHARM power cable / bus. Feeds stage-1 EDF, stage-2 microwave farm / compressor, and stage-3 water plasma thruster.

children.label: Engine housing / nacelle
children.note: Engine nacelle / fairing blended to fuselage. Carries external scoop lips in the OML; opens for skid service.

children.label: External air scoops / variable inlets

ports.note: Bifurcation to stage-1 EDF when in fan mode

children.note: OML-facing air scoops (belly / cheek) with close-off shutters. This is the outside-air capture — NOT the EDF face. Scoops feed an inlet plenum/duct; shutters seal for stage-3 / reentry.

children.label: Inlet duct / plenum
children.note: Internal ducting from external scoops into the engine skid. Splits to (1) stage-1 EDF face and (2) stage-2 precompressor. EDF is in-duct — not a bare fan hanging on the skid nose.

children.label: Shared flared exhaust nozzle
children.note: Common aft exit for ALL three stages: stage-1 EDF bypass + stage-2 air plasma + stage-3 water plasma. Substantial outward flare / C-D contour. Exits under Tail through cradle cutout; Tail does not own it. Not a tiny stub pipe.

ports.note: Stage-1 EDF bypass thrust tube into shared aft exhaust

children.label: Tail assembly
Vertical stabilizer
children.note: Physical fin. Roots to fuselage cradle around the engine nozzle clearance. No joint to the nozzle — the nozzle belongs to the combined-cycle engine.

children.label: Left rudder / speed-brake panel
children.note: Shuttle-style split rudder panel. Together with the right panel: same deflection = yaw; open like a book = speed brake.

children.label: Right rudder / speed-brake panel
children.note: Shuttle-style split rudder panel. Together with the left panel: same deflection = yaw; open like a book = speed brake.
Vertical stabilizer + split rudder panels. Bolted to the fuselage cradle around the top of the engine nozzle opening. Does not own or connect to the nozzle.

children.label: Wing
children.note: Collection: mono-wing body, elevons, and main landing gear. The physical wing bolts to the fuselage cradle belly saddle.

children.label: Mono-wing body
children.note: Single left–right wing structure / wing box.

ports.note: Wing body upper face → fuselage belly saddle

children.label: Left elevon
children.note: Shuttle-style elevon (combined roll/pitch). Trailing edge of left wing.

children.label: Right elevon
children.note: Shuttle-style elevon (combined roll/pitch). Trailing edge of right wing.

children.label: Main landing gear
children.note: Optional sub-kit: left and right main gear joined as one assembly, then mated to the wing mount points — or each leg mated alone. Shuttle mains live in the wing, not the fuselage belly.
